title: The Oldest Song: Hurrian Hymn No. 6
summary: About 3,400 years ago, someone in the city of Ugarit (in modern Syria) pressed a hymn to the goddess Nikkal into clay, along with instructions for a singer and a nine-stringed lyre. Nobody agrees how to read the notation, so every reconstruction you hear today is a different guess.
thumbnailAlt: Thumbnail: a glowing clay tablet and an ancient lyre, titled The Oldest Song

title: The Dancing Plague of 1518
summary: In the summer of 1518, people in Strasbourg started dancing and couldn't stop. The city's "cure"? Hire musicians, build a stage, and keep them dancing. Historians still argue about why it happened.
thumbnailAlt: Thumbnail: a woodcut-style crowd dancing in a medieval Strasbourg street under the cathedral spire

title: Why Van Halen Banned Brown M&M's
summary: Van Halen's tour rider really did demand M&M's, with "absolutely no brown ones." David Lee Roth says it was a safety test hidden in the technical pages: if he found a brown M&M backstage, the promoter hadn't read the fine print, so the crew rechecked the whole stage. Skeptics say it was also great publicity.
thumbnailAlt: Thumbnail: bowls of colorful candy with the words No Brown M&M's, Why Van Halen really banned them

title: The 639-Year Concert
summary: An organ in a German church has been playing John Cage's "As Slow As Possible" since 2001, and it isn't due to finish until 2640. Sandbags hold the keys down, and the chord changes only on rare scheduled days, when crowds come to hear a pipe added or removed.
